figures.finding: The employer deducts Advance Personal Income Tax monthly from a resident's (or a Sri Lankan citizen non-resident's) primary employment pay under Tax Table 1: nothing up to LKR 150,000 a month, then 6% of monthly pay less 9,000 to 233,333, 18% less 37,000 to 275,000, 24% less 53,500 to 316,667, 30% less 72,500 to 358,333 and 36% less 94,000 above; the tables stand for later years until replaced. From the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act No. 11 of 2026 the withholding on service fees paid to resident individuals in s. 85(1C)(c) names artists, actors, singers, musicians, writers and similar professions (its rate was not found).

figures.finding: An employee pays at least 8% of total monthly earnings to the Employees' Provident Fund and the employer at least 12% (20% in all), and the employer alone pays 3% of total monthly earnings to the Employees' Trust Fund; there is no ceiling in the rules read.
figures.applies: Employees in Sri Lanka (EPF Act and ETF Act No. 46 of 1980); self-employed may join the ETF voluntarily

sources.said: Employee’s Contribution: A minimum of 8% of the total monthly earnings (To be deducted from the employee’s salary/wage) Employer’s Contribution: A minimum amount equivalent to 12% of total monthly earnings of the employee (To be paid totally by the employer) Total Contribution per Employee: 20% of the employee’s total monthly earnings
Employer's Contribution 3% of the total monthly earnings (not to be deducted from the employee’s monthly salary / wages)

figures.finding: VAT is 18% from 1 January 2024; registration is required once taxable supplies (other than financial services) exceed LKR 15 million in a quarter or LKR 60 million in twelve months, and anyone making taxable supplies may register voluntarily.
